news.admin module

Admin site configuration for the NewsNow application.

This module registers and customizes the Django administration interface for users, publishers, articles, newsletters, and article approval logs.

The custom user administration configuration extends Django’s built-in UserAdmin to support NewsNow-specific user roles and subscription relationships.

class news.admin.CustomUserAdmin(model, admin_site)[source]

Bases: UserAdmin

Customize the Django admin interface for NewsNow users.

Extends Django’s built-in UserAdmin by adding NewsNow-specific fields to the user administration screen, including user roles, publisher subscriptions, and journalist subscriptions.

Variables:

fieldsets (tuple) – Additional fieldsets displayed in the Django admin interface.

fieldsets = ((None, {'fields': ('username', 'password')}), ('Personal info', {'fields': ('first_name', 'last_name', 'email')}), ('Permissions', {'fields': ('is_active', 'is_staff', 'is_superuser', 'groups', 'user_permissions')}), ('Important dates', {'fields': ('last_login', 'date_joined')}), ('NewsNow', {'fields': ('role', 'subscribed_publishers', 'subscribed_journalists')}))

news.api_views module

API views for the NewsNow application.

This module provides REST API endpoints for managing articles, retrieving subscribed content, approving articles, and processing approved article webhook notifications.

The API supports authenticated access for article management, role-based permissions, editorial approval workflows, and integration with external systems through webhook endpoints.

news.apps module

Application configuration for the NewsNow application.

This module defines the Django application configuration for the NewsNow app and ensures that signal handlers are registered when the application starts.

The configuration is responsible for loading model signal registrations used throughout the application.

class news.apps.NewsConfig(app_name, app_module)[source]

Bases: AppConfig

Configure the NewsNow Django application.

Defines application metadata and performs startup initialization tasks, including registration of model signal handlers.

Variables:

  • default_auto_field (str) – Default type for automatically generated primary keys.

  • name (str) – Django application label.

default_auto_field = 'django.db.models.BigAutoField'
name = 'news'
ready()[source]

Register application signal handlers.

Imports the application’s signal module when Django finishes loading installed applications. Importing the module ensures that all signal receivers are registered before the application begins processing requests.

None

news.forms module

Form definitions for the NewsNow application.

This module provides forms for article management, newsletter creation, publisher management, user registration, and user authentication.

The forms include Bootstrap styling and validation rules specific to the NewsNow platform.

news.models module

Data models for the NewsNow application.

This module defines the core data structures used throughout the application, including publishers, users, articles, newsletters, and approved article logs.

The models implement role-based user management, article approval workflows, publisher membership validation, and newsletter distribution functionality.

news.permissions module

Custom permission classes for the NewsNow application.

This module provides role-based access control for API endpoints used to manage articles and editorial approval workflows.

Permissions determine which users may view, create, update, delete, or approve articles based on their assigned role.

class news.permissions.ArticleRolePermission[source]

Bases: BasePermission

Control access to article resources based on user roles.

Readers may view approved articles, journalists may create and manage their own articles, and editors have unrestricted access to article management operations.

has_object_permission(request, view, obj)[source]

Determine whether the user can access a specific article.

Readers can access only approved articles. Editors have unrestricted access. Journalists may modify only articles that they authored.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – Incoming HTTP request.

  • view (APIView) – Current API view.

  • obj (Article) – Article instance being accessed.

Returns:

True if access is permitted, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

has_permission(request, view)[source]

Determine whether the user has permission to access the view.

Read operations are available to all users. Article creation is restricted to journalists. Update and delete operations are limited to journalists and editors.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – Incoming HTTP request.

  • view (APIView) – Current API view.

Returns:

True if the user has view-level permission, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

class news.permissions.IsEditor[source]

Bases: BasePermission

Restrict access to editor users.

Grants access only to authenticated users whose role is set to EDITOR.

has_permission(request, view)[source]

Determine whether the authenticated user is an editor.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – Incoming HTTP request.

  • view (APIView) – Current API view.

Returns:

True if the authenticated user is an editor, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

news.serializers module

Serializers for the NewsNow application.

This module provides serializers used by the REST API to convert model instances into JSON representations and validate incoming request data.

Serializers are provided for users, publishers, articles, newsletters, and approved article log records.

news.signals module

Signal handlers for the NewsNow application.

This module contains Django signal receivers responsible for automatic group assignment, role-based permission management, article distribution, and webhook notifications.

Signal handlers are triggered by migration and model save events to ensure that application data, permissions, and notifications remain synchronized.

news.signals.assign_group_and_token(sender, instance, created, **kwargs)[source]

Assign role-based group membership to a user.

Updates the user’s Django group assignment whenever the user record is saved. Non-reader users have subscription relationships removed automatically.

Parameters:

  • sender (type) – Model class that triggered the signal.

  • instance (User) – User instance being saved.

  • created (bool) – Indicates whether the user was newly created.

  • kwargs (dict) – Additional signal arguments supplied by Django.

Returns:

None

Return type:

None

news.signals.create_role_groups(sender, **kwargs)[source]

Create and configure NewsNow role groups.

Initializes the Reader, Editor, and Journalist groups after database migrations and assigns the appropriate Django permissions to each role.

Parameters:

  • sender (AppConfig) – Application configuration that triggered the signal.

  • kwargs (dict) – Additional signal arguments supplied by Django.

Returns:

None

Return type:

None

news.signals.distribute_approved_article(sender, instance, **kwargs)[source]

Distribute approved articles and notify subscribers.

Sends email notifications to subscribed readers and publishes approval information to the configured webhook endpoint.

Processing occurs only once per article approval.

Parameters:

  • sender (type) – Model class that triggered the signal.

  • instance (Article) – Article instance being processed.

  • kwargs (dict) – Additional signal arguments supplied by Django.

Returns:

None

Return type:

None

Raises:

requests.RequestException – Raised if the webhook request fails. The exception is handled internally and does not interrupt signal processing.

news.tests module

Automated tests for the NewsNow application.

This module contains unit and integration tests covering REST API endpoints, role-based permissions, web views, signal processing, email notifications, newsletter management, and approved article webhook integrations.

The tests verify application behaviour for readers, journalists, editors, and anonymous users.
